note: Omni Analytics, the BI and AI analytics platform (San Francisco); the same company as the base row omni-analytics (exploreomni.com was its earlier domain). Omni's own release of 2022-08-16 names GV in the $9.4M Seed led by First Round and in the $17.5M Series A led by Redpoint; the firm's /ai list dates its first investment 2022-04 and a re-investment 2022-08, so GV entered at the Seed (entry date from the /ai list, decisions D7) and the named Series A graduates it. Momentum check 2026-09-28: Omni's own release of 2026-04-23 reports a $120M Series C at a $1.5B valuation led by ICONIQ with GV participating, so 1b_plus. The First Round and Redpoint rows still read below_1b; ICONIQ's row carries the same $1.5B mark. The y-combinator row named Omni is a different company (a YC batch company).

Vectorized is Redpanda Data under its first name (streaming data platform, San Francisco); the same company as the base row redpanda. TechCrunch (2021-01-26) splits the $15.5M announcement into a $3M seed led by Lightspeed and a $12.5M Series A from Lightspeed with Google Ventures, and the firm's own posts say GV has led or co-led every round 'since the Series A' (https://www.gv.com/news/redpanda-performance-ai-revolution); the firm's /ai list dates GV's first investment 2020-11 (decisions D7). Mark: the $100M Series D led by GV in April 2025 at a $1 billion valuation (Redpanda's own press page), aligned with the Lightspeed row. Momentum check 2026-09-28: no later priced round in the news search through September 2026.

Trucode Gene Repair is Vera Therapeutics under an earlier name: the S-1's corporate history says it was incorporated as CDF Therapeutics in May 2016, renamed Trucode Gene Repair in October 2017 and Vera Therapeutics in April 2020, at the same 170 Harbor Way, South San Francisco office the archived trucodegene.com shows; the same company as the base row vera-therapeutics. The S-1's principal-stockholder table shows GV's first shares are Series B preferred held by GV 2017, L.P. (Series C through GV 2019, L.P.; no GV Seed or Series A shares), bought in the financing Kleiner Perkins and GV drove in September 2019 (Fierce Biotech, the $34M round at launch): Growth. Public since May 2021: market cap $2.34B on 2026-09-28 (stockanalysis). HQ Brisbane, California, the current SEC business address.

Ridesharing marketplace (San Francisco). GV co-led the $10M Series A with Lightspeed (TechCrunch, 2012-10-10); the late-2011 seed's investors listed there do not include GV. Sidecar stopped rides and deliveries at the end of December 2015, and in January 2016 General Motors acquired certain assets and IP and hired about 20 staff (TechCrunch 2016-01-19; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidecar_%28company%29): a sale of the business's assets after it ceased operating reads acquired, so the prefilled defunct (a Wikidata dissolution) is disputed. Aligned with the Lightspeed and USV rows.

funding_rounds.lead: Lightspeed Venture Partners and Google Ventures

note: Mobile email and sales productivity app (San Francisco, per SugarCRM's release). $3.25M seed from Google Ventures, SoftTech, Freestyle, Foundation Capital, ENIAC and angels (TechCrunch, 2014-04-24). SugarCRM acquired its IP and other assets and hired its engineers in March 2015, shutting the app (https://techcrunch.com/2015/03/08/sugarcrm-buys-mobile-startup-stitch-shuts-it-down/). The other books' Stitch rows (a16z, General Catalyst, y-combinator's London Stitch Technologies, Ribbit's Cape Town fintech) are different companies. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Rumble Entertainment (Rumble Games, rumblegames.com), the free-to-play games developer and publisher, not Rumble Inc. (NASDAQ: RUM): the prefilled public status and $1.73B float are a name join onto the video platform and are disputed. Rumble closed a $15M Series A from Google Ventures and Khosla Ventures (TechCrunch, 2011-12-01; the company was founded that year on a few million dollars of seed money, investors not named). Plarium acquired Rumble in September 2017 (https://www.pocketgamer.biz/plarium-acquires-alliance-heroes-of-the-spire-developer-rumble-entertainment/, terms undisclosed); in July 2024 its later owner Forte shut the studio, by then called R Studios (https://www.gamesindustry.biz/forte-shuts-down-rumble-entertainment-its-second-studio-closure-in-two-months). Status is the last known state, the 2024 closure: defunct, aligned with the Khosla row.

Retail price-tracking site from AngelPad's second class. Undisclosed seed round from Google Ventures, AOL Ventures, Jump Ventures and others (TechCrunch, 2011-06-16). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and shopobot.com is a domain for sale (checked 2026-09-28). No source read places the company in a city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Restaurant-ordering API from the 2011 TechStars NYC class. Its CEO announced a seed round from Google Ventures led by Rich Miner at the TechStars New York demo day (TechCrunch, 2011-10-18). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and ordr.in answers 410 Gone (checked 2026-09-28). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Mobile learning games for preschool children. $325K seed from Google Ventures, 500 Startups and other investors (TechCrunch, 2011-10-12). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and stickeryapp.com no longer answers (checked 2026-09-28). No source read places the company in a city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Traveler-to-local matching site, home base San Francisco. TechCrunch names its $1M round a Series A with Google Ventures, GRP Partners, Launchpad LA, 500 Startups and Idealab among investors (2012-03-08; $1.3M raised in total, so a smaller earlier raise exists whose investors are not named), and repeats 'its $1 million Series A ... from Google Ventures' when the team relaunched as the Wist app in November 2013 (https://techcrunch.com/2013/11/22/travel-startup-triptrotting-relaunches-as-wist-a-local-recommendations-app-for-iphone/). The firm's own posts show nothing earlier. Fate after the Wist relaunch unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and triptrotting.com is parked (checked 2026-09-28).

Online shopping wish-list tool from the 2011 TechStars NYC class (its December 2011 Form D, $859,998 sold of $999,999, was filed from 8 Spruce Street, New York). $1M seed led by RRE Ventures with Google Ventures, Quotidian Ventures and New York angels (TechCrunch, 2012-08-09). In 2013 it launched the Fresh app; by 2014 its CTO and creative director had joined Nifti (TechCrunch, 2014-09-25). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and wantworthy.com is parked (checked 2026-09-28). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Kids' clothing subscription launched out of Los Angeles's Science incubator in January 2012. 'Wittlebee raised a $2.5 million seed round from Google Ventures, Matt Coffin, Crosslink Capital, and Rincon Venture Partners' (TechCrunch, 2013-05-13); no source read dates the seed itself, so no entry date is written. The same article reports the co-founder CEO stepping down after it could not raise a Series A. Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and wittlebee.com no longer answers (checked 2026-09-28). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Price-tracking shopping tool founded by Tuck MBA graduates, with an office in Boston's North End. Tuck's article of 2013-07-24 says the founders secured $800,000 from Google Ventures and angel investors (the seed; seed investors also named). TechCrunch (2014-09-25) reports $1.2M more in seed funding in December 2013 and the Cinch polling app spun out in 2014 (https://techcrunch.com/2014/09/25/price-tracking-service-nifti-switches-gears-launches-social-polling-app-cinch/). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and nifti.com shows an empty directory (checked 2026-09-28). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Predictive personal-assistant iPhone app, launched as Sherpa and renamed Osito in April 2013 (https://techcrunch.com/2013/04/18/goodbye-sherpa-hello-osito-predictive-intelligence-ios-app-rebrands-and-graduates-from-beta/). $1.1M seed from Andreessen Horowitz, Google Ventures, InterWest, Merus, Innovation Endeavors and AngelPad (TechCrunch, 2013-03-25). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown; getosito.com shows a placeholder page (checked 2026-09-28). No source read places the company in a city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Shelf.com, a product-cataloguing and resale site from San Francisco, founded by Dayo Esho and Chris Kline. 'Shelf is backed by $1.2 million in seed funding led by Google Ventures back in 2014' (TechCrunch, 2016-01-27). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and shelf.com shows an empty page (checked 2026-09-28). The insight-partners row named Shelf is a different company (Shelf.io, the Stamford knowledge-management firm). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Same-day prescription delivery covering the Bay Area in 2015. $5M seed from 8 Partners, Google Ventures, StartX and angels (TechCrunch, 2015-11-17). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown; tinyrx.com now serves a telehealth prescription business, and no source read ties it to this company (checked 2026-09-28). The article names the Bay Area, not a city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Activity-planning app that launched at TechCrunch Disrupt in 2011. GV's round: an undisclosed amount led by Google Ventures with Slow Ventures and TenOneTen, all new investors (TechCrunch, 2013-05-30); no source names the round, so the stage is undetermined. Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and weotta.com refuses the request (checked 2026-09-28). No source read places the company in a city.

Autism blood-test developer (Massachusetts). Google Ventures led a $15.4M round in July 2013, joined by Foundation Medical Partners and earlier investors North Bridge and General Catalyst (TechCrunch, 2013-07-22). The record does not name the round, but the company's own Form Ds show it was its second priced round: $9.35M sold from 2010-05-26 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1492969/000149296910000001/0001492969-10-000001-index.htm, the round the BCV and General Catalyst rows entered) and then $15.35M sold from 2013-07-18 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1492969/000149296913000002/0001492969-13-000002-index.htm), above the era's $15M Series A band: a Series B by position, so Growth (model, medium). HQ Lexington, Massachusetts, the 2013 filing address (the siblings' Waltham is the 2010 address). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown after 2014, aligned with the BCV and General Catalyst rows.

Restaurant staff-performance software (MUSE), Boston. GV's round on record: $1.5M in November 2011 led by Atlas Venture with Google Ventures, NextView, Canary and angels (FinSMEs, read from its archived copy); the report names no round, and Fortune says the company raised about $9M of equity and debt from 2010, so the stage is undetermined. In June 2015 Bit9 hired about a dozen of its staff in an acqui-hire; the core IP was not included, the CEO retired and the company began winding down its customers (https://fortune.com/2015/06/15/exclusive-bit9-acquires-objective-logistics/). An acqui-hire decides nothing; the company wound down, so defunct.

Ready (Ready Responders, readyresponders.com), in-home urgent care founded in New Orleans in 2016; the prefilled GB is a one-word name match and is disputed. GV was among the investors in its $54M Series C (Home Health Care News, 2020-09-16; valuation above $350M per Bloomberg as quoted there); the article says GV, Deerfield and City Light invested over $100M across two rounds in under a year, so GV may already have been in the preceding round, also Growth. It now operates as myLaurel: readyresponders.com serves myLaurel's site, the firm's own listing replaced Ready with myLaurel in 2023 under the same partner, and myLaurel's November 2025 round names Deerfield and GV as previous investors (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/steelsky-ventures-leads-investment-in-mylaurel-to-redefine-acute-and-transitional-care-at-home-302607293.html). myLaurel gives its headquarters as New York (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mylaurel-positioned-to-save-us-hospitals-billions-by-maximizing-hospital-efficiency-and-enhancing-patient-outcomes-302071798.html); it still operates in New Orleans. The same company as the base row mylaurel. The y-combinator row named Ready is a different company (a fintech).

Seafood trading marketplace, headquartered in Edinburgh (Tech.eu, Insider). Index Ventures led the $23M Series A with GV and Point Nine participating (TechCrunch, 2022-04-24; before it, Point Nine and Eos Advisory funded the seed), so GV entered at the Series A. Status aligned with the Point Nine row, whose firm lists the company as closed; rooser.eu no longer resolves (checked 2026-09-28).

Studio of America, Inc. (s-tud.io), a New York maker of a group video app and, by 2026, a creative studio; the prefilled DK is a one-word name match and is disputed. $3.3M seed led by GV's M.G. Siegler, with Mercury Fund and Pareto (TechCrunch, 2022-09-29, 'New York-based Studio'; the same three co-founders appear on the company's own team page). Private: its site was live in the 2026-02-11 capture (http://web.archive.org/web/20260211220909/https://s-tud.io/); the domain did not resolve on 2026-09-28. The y-combinator row named Studio is a different company. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Furnished flexible-rental operator, San Francisco (Dogpatch). It was winding down operations in November 2023 (TechCrunch 2023-11-08, citing The Information; the San Francisco Chronicle reported the same). No source read ties GV to a round: TechCrunch names Initialized (seed and Series A leads), Airbnb in the 2019 $55M Series B at $205M, and SIG leading the October 2021 $55M round, without GV; the firm's listing runs 2019 to 2023. Stage undetermined.

Character-driven toys, animation and synthetic-influencer company founded by Paul Budnitz; its Form Ds are filed from 47 Maple Street, Burlington, Vermont. GV led a $6M round in October 2020 (VirtualHumans.org, 2020-10-22), but the sources disagree on what came before and after: that article calls the July 2019 $10M round a Series A, while TechCrunch calls the October 2021 $20M round the Series A (https://techcrunch.com/2021/10/20/superplastic-guggimon-janky-virtual-celebrities-series-a/). The GV round is unnamed and cannot be placed on either side of a Series A, so the stage is undetermined. Later: a $20M round led by Amazon in February 2023 (https://techcrunch.com/2023/02/15/superplastic-a-creator-of-synthetic-influencers-raises-20m-led-by-amazon-in-deal-to-make-tv-shows-and-more/). No priced mark near $1B is reported.

Primary care for adults over 65 in the Philadelphia area (Form D address 150 Monument Road, Bala Cynwyd). 'Andreessen Horowitz and Alphabet's GV co-led Patina's seed and Series A funding', $57M in total (Business Insider, 2021-10-26); the company's Form Ds date the $7M seed from 2020-10-08 (two investors) and the $50M Series A from 2021-10-22 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1891732/000189173221000002/0001891732-21-000002-index.htm). The named Series A graduates the seed. The practice closed: its own site now carries the records custodian's notice that Patina Medical Group stopped providing care on 2025-09-30 'due to unforeseen business challenges' (https://patinahealth.com). The a16z row still reads private.

Programmable genomic integration (gene insertion) company in Watertown, Massachusetts (its launch release's dateline). It launched in December 2023 having raised $213M 'in Series A and B funding' from a16z, ARCH, GV, Longwood, Polaris and others (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2023/12/12/2794660/0/en/tome-biosciences-launches-with-over-200-million-in-funding-to-advance-programmable-genomic-integration-platform.html); neither the release nor BioSpace says which of the two rounds GV joined, so the stage is undetermined. In August 2024 it filed notice to lay off virtually its entire staff from November 1, planning to wind down and seek a buyer (https://www.statnews.com/2024/08/23/tome-biosciences-files-notice-to-lay-off-nearly-entire-staff/); no sale is reported, so defunct, aligned with the a16z row (whose Cambridge city is not what the company's own releases give).

Small-molecule cancer and inflammation biotech, Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its Form Ds show rounds from 2015 onward; the July 2021 $65M round was led by Deerfield and US Venture Partners with existing investors named (Globes, 2021-07-15), and no source read names GV in any round (the firm lists it from 2021), so the stage is undetermined. Ribon discontinued all material operations and auctioned substantially all of its assets (its IP) in 2024, with no buyer named (https://www.biospace.com/business/big-pharma-backed-ribon-therapeutics-shuts-down-business-operations): defunct.

note: Next Autoworks (formerly V-Vehicle), a San Diego car startup backed by Kleiner Perkins, T. Boone Pickens and Google Ventures, with about $100M from investors (Greentech Media, http://web.archive.org/web/20250817115321/https://www.greentechmedia.com/articles/read/next-autoworks-the-curse-of-the-doe-loan-guarantee). The DOE refused its $320M loan in November 2011; it closed its San Diego headquarters and cut staff in December 2011 (Automotive News, http://web.archive.org/web/20200308025243/https://www.autonews.com/article/20111219/OEM/111219864/startup-next-autoworks-scales-back-after-failing-to-secure-u-s-loan), and the local paper of its planned Louisiana plant wrote in 2014 that the deal died with the loan (https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/money/2014/12/20/davison-crossroad-guide-facilitys-future/20670315/). No later activity is reported: defunct. No source read names the round GV joined, so the stage is undetermined.

Machine-learning analytics for health plans, Burlington, Massachusetts (its 2013 and 2014 Form D address). Welltok acquired it in May 2015 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/welltok-acquires-leading-healthcare-analytics-company-predilytics-300085640.html). Its Form Ds show rounds of $6.07M (from 2012-08-16), $4.5M (from 2013-09-18) and $8.9M (from 2014-11-24), none naming a GV person, and no source read names the round GV joined (the firm lists it 2013 to 2015), so the stage is undetermined.

In vivo delivery platforms for genetic medicines from the Liu and Joung labs. At its April 2024 launch GEN reported '$100 million in seed funding, raised two years ago' from Newpath, Atlas, F-Prime and 5AM 'with participation from GV (Google Ventures) and ARCH', so GV entered at the Seed (entry year 2022). In December 2024 it merged with Chroma Medicine into nChroma Bio, led by Nvelop's CEO, with $75M of new funding (https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/chroma-nvelop-merge-epigenetic-editing-nchroma-walsh-liu/735189/): a merger into a successor reads acquired. Fierce calls both 'Boston-area biotechs'; no source read gives Nvelop's own municipality. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Rally.org (formerly Piryx), a social fundraising and payments platform headquartered in San Francisco's SoMa. Its 2011 seed came from Floodgate, Greylock Discovery and Ron Conway (https://techcrunch.com/2011/06/16/social-fundraising-platform-piryx-is-reborn-as-rally-org-with-top-investors-in-tow/), no GV. Forbes (2013-02-13, read from its archived copy) tells how the May 2012 Series A came together: Floodgate, Reid Hoffman and Eric Ries leading with $3.5M and 18 more backers adding $4.4M; Kevin Rose, then a new Google Ventures partner, said yes, the CEO met 'Kevin Rose and Google Ventures in Mountain View' on May 24, and the round closed on May 25. The firm lists Rally from 2013 with Kevin Rose as its partner. Series A at medium confidence (the article does not list the round's final investors). Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown, and rally.org is parked (checked 2026-09-28). The accel and battery-ventures rows named Rally are different companies.

No source read names the round GV joined (the firm lists it from 2013), so the stage is undetermined. The a16z and General Catalyst Rabbit rows are identity-unresolved; if either is rabb.it it should read acquired too.

AI oncology practice-workflow platform (therapy selection, insurance pre-approval, care coordination); its own site gives 7300 Sandlake Commons Blvd, Orlando (https://www.oncologic.ai). On the firm's live list with partner David Reshef. No source read names a round or ties GV to one, so the stage is undetermined. Momentum check 2026-09-28 (Google News for the company's name with 'raises'; the results are the common word, not the company): no priced round near $1B reported, so below_1b.

Synapse Health, the durable-medical-equipment ordering platform, 1603 Orrington Avenue, Evanston, Illinois (both Form Ds). Its Form Ds show $15M sold from 2022-12-20 (14 investors) and $25M sold of a $45M offering from 2023-09-11 (one investor); Ben Robbins of GV is a director on both, the second filed from GV's Mountain View address. Operating in 2026 (Business Wire, 2026-02-17: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260217562789/en/Synapse-Health-to-Lead-Medtrade-2026-Panel-on-the-Future-of-Value-Based-Contracting-in-DME). No priced mark near $1B is reported. Membership stays medium (a seat, not a listing).

Women-focused coworking clubs, New York. GV was not in the $75M Series C of December 2018 (led by Sequoia with Upfront, Airbnb, NEA and WeWork: https://www.businessinsider.com/women-only-coworking-space-the-wing-just-raised-75-million-led-by-sequoia-capital-2018-12). In January 2020 WeWork sold its minority stake to a consortium of new and existing investors including GV (CNBC, 2020-01-22; Business Insider says the group was led by GV, at a $165M valuation plus a $15M convertible note: https://www.businessinsider.com/the-wings-valuation-plummeted-with-sale-of-wework-stake-2020-3): a secondary, so Growth. IWG bought a majority stake in February 2021 (https://www.businessinsider.com/iwg-ceo-mark-dixon-majority-stake-the-wing-coworking-startup-2021-2) and The Wing closed on 2022-08-31 (https://observer.com/2022/08/women-only-club-the-wing-shuts-down-leaving-event-partners-and-furniture-lovers-in-the-lurch/). Status is the last known state: defunct, aligned with the Sequoia row.

Place (place.xyz) is the community-network product Backplane pivoted to in 2015; the same company as the base row backplane (listed 2012 to 2015 under the same partner, David Krane). 'GV, then called Google Ventures, was among the investors in the company's 2011 seed round ... The seed investors returned for a $12.1m series A round the following year' (Global Venturing, 2016-04-15), so Seed, graduated by the named Series A. In April 2016 Backplane went out of business and sold its assets through Dorsey & Whitney while some Series A investors set up a new company to relaunch the business (same source; https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2016/04/lady-gaga-backplane-start-up-meets-an-untimely-end): an asset sale out of insolvency with a successor reads acquired.

basis: Merger consideration, not an investment (COLLECTION.md s1, the share-swap reading of the sale-consideration rule): GV's company here was Moonfrye (listed 2013 to 2014, a row of its own), renamed P.S. XO, which merged with the New Zealand toy and craft company Seedling in October 2014; the combined company kept the Seedling name, Seedling had never taken outside money, and the $7M raised with the merger came from Upfront Ventures and Greycroft, not GV (TechCrunch, 2014-10-29). The firm lists Seedling from 2015, right after its Moonfrye listing ends. Moonfrye stays the member. Flagged for Erik: the parties called it a merger of equals.

note: Hands-free enterprise software for Google Glass and other wearables. Fate unknown: no source read reports a sale or shutdown. The First Round row says it 'became Proxy', but Proxy was incorporated separately as Martians Inc. (TechCrunch, 2016-08-22), so that reading is not followed; the a16z row also reads unknown.

Anonymous group-chat app. 'Raising an $800,000 seed back in October, led by Khosla Ventures' Ben Ling. Google Ventures' MG Siegler also participated in the round' (TechCrunch, 2014-03-25); the firm lists rumr 2014 to 2015 with Siegler as partner. Status and city aligned with the Khosla row (the app shut down; rumrapp.com is a domain for sale, checked 2026-09-28). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Token-based monetization platform for mobile game developers (the firm's own 2012 listing). No source read names a round or ties GV to one; Google News returns only the common phrase. Status and city aligned with the First Round row (defunct, San Francisco); pocketchange.com no longer answers (checked 2026-09-28).

Crowd-sourced credit circles ('a new way to access credit', the firm's 2015 listing). No source read names a round or the company's fate; Google News returns only the common word. Status and city aligned with the a16z row; puddle.com no longer answers (checked 2026-09-28).

Scout, a contextual Android home-screen launcher (scoutlauncher.com). Its own About page names founders Nikhil Chandhok (nine years at Google, then Entrepreneur in Residence at Google Ventures) and Kunal Punera (RelateIQ, Yahoo) and no UK tie; the prefilled GB is a one-word Wikidata match and is disputed (US, from the founders' record; the page gives no city). No source read names a round or the company's fate; scoutlauncher.com is a domain for sale (checked 2026-09-28).

Super.cc, an email-to-calendar service built by Michael Galpert (a founder of Aviary), launched in February 2014 (https://techcrunch.com/2014/02/10/super-cc/); its parent Superhuman had 'raised some seed capital' by May 2013 (TechCrunch), no investors named, so the stage is undetermined. No source read gives its fate or city; super.cc is a domain for sale (checked 2026-09-28).

Maker of the Prep Pad smart kitchen scale. Maker of the MovieGoer social moviegoing iPhone app (co-founder Brian Dear). TechCrunch (2012-02-08) says it 'has raised funding from Google Ventures, 500 Startups and others' without naming the round, so the stage is undetermined. No source read gives its city or fate.

Lead-generation and free mobile web pages for local businesses (its own site in a January 2016 capture, http://web.archive.org/web/20160130073452/https://newhound.com/).
